images.title: 8 rows of 13 cut in the middle and put side by side
images.purpose: Show that cutting 8 rows of 13 across the middle and putting the two blocks side by side makes 4 rows of 26 with the same 104 packets.
images.composition: An array of 8 rows of 13 with a dashed cut line on the left, an arrow, and the two halves side by side as 4 rows of 26 on the right, with both number sentences and the words Half and Double.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the left, one array of exactly 104 butter packets in 8 rows of 13 columns, cut across the middle. Every packet is a square 26 by 26 px (corner radius 4 px) with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and no marking; neighbouring packets are 4 px apart across and down. The array's top left corner is at x 82 and y 290 and it spans x 82 to 468 and y 290 to 526. Its top 4 rows (52 packets) are filled teal #0072B2 and its bottom 4 rows (52 packets) are filled amber #E69F00. A dashed vermilion #D55E00 cut line (4 px) runs across the middle between row 4 and row 5 at y 408, from x 66 to x 484, with a small dark scissors symbol at its left end. At the right, one array of exactly 104 packets in 4 rows of 26 columns, made of the two blocks side by side: the left block is 4 rows of 13 packets filled teal, top left corner at x 588 and y 350, spanning x 588 to 974 and y 350 to 466; the right block is 4 rows of 13 packets filled amber, top left corner at x 994 and y 350, spanning x 994 to 1380 and y 350 to 466; the two blocks are 20 px apart. Between the arrays, centred at y 408, one grey #6B7280 arrow (5 px line, pointing right) from x 500 to x 575. In dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif: above the left array the sentence 8 × 13 = 104, centred at x 275 and y 235 (44 px); above the right array the sentence 4 × 26 = 104, centred at x 984 and y 305 (44 px); under the right array, centred at x 984, the line Half: 8 rows become 4 rows at y 540 and the line Double: 13 columns become 26 columns at y 590 (34 px each). In all there are 208 packets, none missing. No other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Halve one number and double the other and the product stays the same: 8 × 13 = 4 × 26 = 104.
images.description: An array of 104 butter packets, 8 rows of 13, cut across the middle and put side by side as 4 rows of 26, with 8 × 13 = 104 and 4 × 26 = 104 written beside them.
images.context: Concept image for Halve One Number, Double the Other. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (a packet array cut in the middle with the halves moved) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 8 and 13.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student count the packets before and after and see that none were added or lost. The slip to watch: halving both numbers, or doubling both, instead of halving one and doubling the other.

image_decisions.why: The array cut in the middle and moved shows why the product stays the same when one number is halved and the other doubled, which words alone do not.
